items.q: And the person you'll hear of all through this session is Ade Monsborough... Don Pixie Roberts is on clarinet. Graham Bell piano... It was recorded in Melbourne on the 6th of August, 1949.

ctx.x: Could you give us the personnel of this early recording and perhaps maybe when it was recorded?

Generally, it was a pretty stable group over quite a long time. And as I said, Roger Bell was on trumpet. And the person you'll hear of all through this session is Ade Monsborough, who probably is Australia's best known musician. And he plays a great range of instruments. And on this record, he plays valve trombone and clarinet. Don Pixie Roberts is on clarinet. Graham Bell piano. Bud Baker banjo and guitar. And Lucille Berison on tuba. And Russ Murphy on drums. It was recorded in Melbourne on the 6th of August,…

And to open the program this evening, we're going to hear just a closer walk with thee by Graham Bell. dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear dear…

Another group that was going at that time was the Southern Jazz Group, who come from Adelaide, which is another capital city of South Australia, which is down next to Victoria, the state in which Melbourne is in. Now, they had a very fine band, and the leader of the band, Dave Dalwitz, was also a composer and composed lots of tunes. And the first one of these we're going to hear is called Emu Strut. This was recorded in 1st of June, 1950. And the members of the band were Bill Munro on trumpet, dug up Ade…
May I ask you, what is an emu?
